nodes.label: Root Nudity Category
nodes.description: Root classification covering all visual depictions of partial or full human nakedness, with relevance to compliance, age-restrictions, product guidelines, and trust & safety policies.

properties.context: This category encompasses any image, video, or digital depiction of a human body in a state of undress, covering both adult and minor situations. The subcategories below address whether it is sexual, non-sexual, or involves special contexts (e.g. art, child-related, non-consensual).
examples: Photographs or videos of nude individuals
Minimal clothing images that verge on nudity
edge_cases: Cultural or ritual nudity (e.g., indigenous practices)
Historic or documentary images where nudity appears incidentally

nodes.label: Explicit Nudity
nodes.description: Depictions where genitals, breasts, or sexual acts are clearly visible and intended to sexually arouse or offend. Common in adult entertainment products, images, or accessories.

properties.context: Adult-oriented content featuring clearly visible breasts (female nipples), genitals, or explicit sexual activities. Often considered pornographic or adult content. May be subject to age restrictions and obscenity laws.
examples: Pornographic magazines showing full frontal nudity
Hardcore videos depicting clear sexual acts
edge_cases: Simulated sex with partial nudity might fall under suggestive vs. explicit
Art photography displaying genitals in an artistic context

nodes.label: Suggestive Nudity
nodes.description: Content where nudity is implied but not directly shown, using poses, partial clothing, or strategic coverage that suggests nakedness.

properties.context: Sexually suggestive content without fully exposed genitals or nipples. Poses, partial or sheer coverage that teases nudity. Can be borderline adult or considered erotic, depending on platform.
examples: Lingerie shoots revealing shape but not explicit detail
Strategically placed objects obscuring genitals
edge_cases: Very small bikini or thong might be borderline explicit vs. just minimal clothing
Body paint covering breasts/genitals could appear effectively nude

nodes.label: Non-Sexual Nudity
nodes.description: Nudity represented in non-sexual contexts such as art, medicine, or educational content. Often requires nuanced classification to distinguish from inappropriate content.

properties.context: Covers all forms of nudity that are not meant to arouse but serve legitimate educational, artistic, or social functions. May still require gating or disclaimers depending on policy.
examples: Medical demonstrations of the human body
Breastfeeding or childbirth images
Cultural or anthropological documentation of indigenous nudity
edge_cases: Borderline artistic vs. erotic photography
Documentary footage of nudity that could be misused

nodes.label: Artistic Nudity
nodes.description: Classical or modern art forms displaying nudity—paintings, sculptures, and installations—often protected under freedom of expression but needs review in retail/online settings.

properties.context: Specifically highlights nudity in artworks, from classical paintings to modern art pieces, usually recognized for cultural or aesthetic value rather than sexual content.
examples: Renaissance sculptures (e.g., Michelangelo’s David)
Gallery exhibitions featuring nude figure drawings
edge_cases: Contemporary art photography that some may interpret as erotic
Performance art that involves partial or full nudity

nodes.label: Child Nudity
nodes.description: Any depiction of underage individuals in states of undress, requiring strict monitoring and often prohibited regardless of context.

properties.context: Covers all nudity of minors (under 18). Even if not sexual, such content is heavily restricted or disallowed to prevent abuse or potential sexual exploitation. Strict legal compliance required.
examples: Family photos showing partially nude children (bathtub pictures)
Documentary footage of unclothed minors in certain cultures
edge_cases: Historic war/famine images including nude children
Incidental background child nudity captured inadvertently

nodes.label: AI/Digitally Altered Nudity
nodes.description: Nudity created or modified using digital tools, AI generation, or manipulation techniques.

properties.context: Content in which nudity is introduced or manipulated via digital means—Photoshop, AI, face-swapping. May be consensual or non-consensual. Can involve synthetic media (deepfakes).
examples: Photoshopped images that remove clothing
AI-generated nude 'art' that never involved a real model
edge_cases: Celebrity deepfakes used for malicious or harassing ends
Cartoonish transformations that are obviously fake vs. realistic manipulations

nodes.label: Fetish or Kink-Based Nudity
nodes.description: Nudity associated with specific sexual preferences, fetishes, or kink communities, often involving specialized clothing, accessories, or scenarios.

properties.context: Content that centers on fetish or BDSM themes rather than 'vanilla' sexual depiction. Legal if adults consent, but it may overlap with extreme or obscene content if violent or bestial.
examples: BDSM imagery featuring restraints, latex clothing, consensual bondage
Foot fetish photography focusing on naked body parts in a fetish context
edge_cases: Severe pain or injury can be mistaken for non-consensual abuse
Bestial or necrophilic fetish is outright disallowed (illegal, obscene)

nodes.label: Contextual Nudity (e.g., bath scenes, medical)
nodes.description: Nudity shown within specific contexts that provide legitimate reasons for the display, such as bathing scenes or medical situations.

properties.context: Nudity displayed for reasons incidental to normal life events (bath, medical exam) or other contexts not primarily sexual. Overlaps with non-sexual if the subject matter is purely functional.
examples: Shower scenes in a film that are not sexually charged
Medical tutorial showing a nude patient for demonstration
edge_cases: Disrobing scenes that could be exploited or reinterpreted as erotic
Soap ads featuring partial nudity in a bathing context

nodes.label: Adult Animated/Cartoon Nudity
nodes.description: Animated or cartoon depictions of adult nudity, including anime, hentai, and adult-oriented cartoons.

properties.context: Cartoon or CGI-based nudity featuring adults in sexual or nude scenarios. Often treated similarly to real adult nudity for rating or gating purposes. If it includes minors (even fictitious), it becomes CSAM or obscene content.
examples: Hentai scenes depicting adult characters in sexual acts
3D animated porn with fantasy creatures (adult content)
edge_cases: Indistinguishable CGI from real humans may trigger stricter moderation
Animated incest or bestial themes become obscene or illegal

nodes.label: Accidental/Unintentional Exposure
nodes.description: Inadvertent exposure of private body parts, often in candid photography, sports events, or wardrobe malfunctions.

properties.context: Images or videos where the subject did not intend to be nude, but a slip or accident occurred. This differs from intentional nudity; distribution may raise privacy issues if non-consensual.
examples: Wardrobe malfunctions at live events
Sports photography capturing brief exposures
edge_cases: Publicly distributed “nip slip” photos could be considered non-consensual intimate content
Subject might not be aware they were photographed in that moment

nodes.label: Film/TV Entertainment Nudity
nodes.description: Nudity portrayed in mainstream film, television, or streaming content for artistic or narrative purposes.

properties.context: Nudity found in commercially produced movies or shows, typically regulated by rating systems (MPAA, TV ratings). Often not pornographic but can be restricted from minors’ view.
examples: R-rated movie scenes with brief topless exposure
TV series featuring sexual content for plot or character development
edge_cases: Extended, graphic sex scenes in mainstream films can border on pornography
Foreign films with cultural norms allowing more frontal nudity

nodes.label: Historical/Documentary Nudity
nodes.description: Nudity presented in historical contexts or documentary materials, often for educational or archival purposes.

properties.context: Images or footage from past eras or real-world events (conflicts, famine, tribal life) where nudity is incidental or part of cultural/historical record. Typically granted more leniency if purely documentary.
examples: Archival war photography containing partially nude subjects
Anthropological films capturing indigenous groups with minimal clothing
edge_cases: Exploitation of historical images for prurient interest
Defining whether the historical context outweighs potential sexualization

nodes.label: Visible Sexual Acts (real or simulated)
nodes.description: Content depicting sexual activities, whether actually performed or simulated.

properties.context: A broad subcategory covering any depiction of intercourse, oral sex, masturbation, or sexual conduct between consenting adults—overlaps with explicit nudity. Possibly subject to age gating or legal restrictions on pornography.
examples: A video of consenting adults engaging in intercourse
Simulated sex scenes in mainstream cinema
edge_cases: Explicit porn vs. softcore scenes with no explicit genital display
Platform differences on what counts as adult sexual content

nodes.label: Nudity through See-Through Apparel
nodes.description: Clothing that is transparent, translucent, or sheer enough to reveal body parts underneath.

properties.context: Covers attire that reveals otherwise private body parts—often considered partial or implied nudity. May be flagged depending on the extent of body reveal.
examples: Sheer lingerie exposing nipples or genitals
Wet t-shirt scenario highlighting breast outlines
edge_cases: Dark vs. light see-through fabrics (some might obscure details)
Stylized runway fashion or art photography

nodes.label: Erotic or Provocative Posing without Direct Exposure
nodes.description: Poses intended to be sexually suggestive without explicit nudity.

properties.context: Covers sexual or alluring body positions that do not necessarily show explicit nudity but strongly imply sexuality or accentuate private areas.
examples: Instagram poses in tight bikinis, focusing on butt or chest
Boudoir photography without direct frontal nudity
edge_cases: Context-driven: a yoga pose vs. an intentionally erotic posture
Overlaps with ‘suggestive nudity’ if near-nude clothing is used

nodes.label: Cartoon/AI Child Nudity
nodes.description: Animated, illustrated, or AI-generated depictions of children in states of undress.

properties.context: Depictions of minors (under 18) in non-real mediums—cartoons, 3D models, or AI—for explicit or non-explicit reasons. Treated with the same caution as real child images due to risk of sexual exploitation or grooming.
examples: Anime featuring underage characters in minimal clothing
AI generated images of a child’s face or body in partial nudity
edge_cases: If content is erotic or sexual, it can be considered CSAM even if no real child was used (PROTECT Act).
Cartoonish stylization might mislead moderation if childlike features are borderline.

nodes.label: Deepfake Nudity (Face Swaps)
nodes.description: Technology-enabled creation of fake nude imagery by swapping faces onto nude bodies.

properties.context: Subcategory of digitally altered content specifically for non-consensual or deceptive uses—someone’s face placed on a nude or sexual image. Often considered a form of harassment or privacy violation.
examples: Celebrity deepfake porn videos posted on adult sites
A revenge porn scenario using AI face-swapping to humiliate the victim
edge_cases: Parody or comedic deepfakes not intended to degrade or sexualize
Technical detection challenges when deepfake is highly realistic

nodes.label: Virtual Nudity (Avatars in Games/VR/Metaverse)
nodes.description: Digital representations of nudity in virtual environments, games, or platforms.

properties.context: Game characters or metaverse avatars that can appear nude or sexual. If intended for adult scenarios (e.g. VR sex simulations), typically subject to adult rating. Distinct from real-life nudity but still regulated on many platforms.
examples: A VR chatroom where users design nude avatars
Role-playing games with explicit sexual character options
edge_cases: Might overlap with child-protection concerns if minors can create or view adult avatars
Moderation difficulty in user-created virtual worlds

nodes.label: Nudity in Medical/Scientific/Educational Context
nodes.description: Nudity presented for educational, scientific, or medical purposes.

properties.context: Explicit or partial nudity used to teach or demonstrate. Common in medical textbooks, documentaries, or anatomy classes. Treated more leniently if non-sexual and purely instructional.
examples: Medical diagrams showing reproductive organs
Educational videos about childbirth or breast exams
edge_cases: May still require adult gating if images are graphic
Online platforms might automatically flag if not clearly labeled as educational

nodes.label: Nudity Depicting Ritual/Cultural Traditions
nodes.description: Traditional or cultural practices involving nudity or minimal clothing that reflects specific cultural contexts.

properties.context: Images or videos from ceremonies, tribes, or historical events in which partial or full nudity is a normal aspect of culture rather than sexual. Often appears in anthropology or documentary media.
examples: Indigenous group ceremonies without western clothing
Historic tribe photos with minimal attire
edge_cases: Potential objectification or voyeurism by viewers outside the culture
Distinguishing legitimate documentary from exploitative fetish content

nodes.label: Non-Consensual Intimate Content
nodes.description: Sexual or nude content that was created or distributed without the subject’s consent, encompassing revenge porn, voyeuristic material, or deepfake porn that violates privacy.

properties.context: Includes any scenario where the depicted individual did not agree to the capture or sharing of their intimate images. Illegal in most U.S. states, and typically a priority removal for platforms.
examples: Hidden-camera recordings in bathrooms
Leaked private sexts posted to humiliate an ex-partner
edge_cases: Original consent to be photographed does not include consent for public posting
Differentiating malicious deepfakes from comedic face-swaps

nodes.label: Sexual Violence / Rape Content
nodes.description: Depictions of rape, sexual assault, or other non-consensual sexual acts, whether real or staged. Typically disallowed in mainstream contexts.

properties.context: Imagery or video showing forced sexual acts. Legally considered extremely harmful content. Platforms generally ban it outright, even if it's a simulated 'fantasy' scenario, due to the depiction of sexual harm.
examples: A porn scene depicting realistic rape or assault
Clips of a drunk or unconscious person being violated
edge_cases: BDSM roleplay can appear non-consensual; context that all parties consented might not override the depiction of forced sex in some policies
Documentary footage evidencing real sexual violence used as legal evidence or news coverage

nodes.label: Extreme or Obscene Pornography
nodes.description: Highly extreme adult sexual content that may be deemed obscene under the Miller test, including bestiality, necrophilia, or incest themes.

properties.context: Covers the most egregious forms of adult sexual content lacking serious value and likely to be considered obscene. Often illegal to distribute. Overlaps with cruelty (e.g. bestiality, necrophilia).
examples: Bestiality videos involving humans and animals
Material depicting necrophilia or incest
Hardcore violent porn with no redeeming artistic or social value
edge_cases: Fictional or animated depictions of these acts are still typically disallowed if considered obscene
Cultural differences in definitions of ‘extreme’ or ‘shock porn’

nodes.label: Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)
nodes.description: Visual content depicting minors in any sexual act or context, unequivocally illegal to produce, distribute, or possess.

properties.context: Covers any sexually explicit depiction of a minor under 18, including actual or simulated acts. Zero tolerance. Strictly illegal and must be removed/reported. Federal laws mandate immediate escalation.
examples: Photos or videos of minors engaged in intercourse or sexual posing
Digitally manipulated images placing a minor’s head on adult porn
edge_cases: Drawn or CG child sexual content is criminally prosecutable if obscene
Sexting among teens still qualifies as production/distribution of child porn

nodes.label: Federal Obscenity Law (Miller Test, 18 U.S.C. §§1460-1466)
nodes.description: Defines and criminalizes obscene adult content lacking literary, artistic, political, or scientific value. Distribution can lead to fines or prison.

properties.context: Applies the Miller test to decide if adult content is obscene and unprotected. Violations can result in prosecution under federal statutes. States also apply local community standards.
examples: Hardcore bestiality or necrophilia content sold online
Certain extreme fetish videos deemed patently offensive
edge_cases: Adult films with some narrative or artistic claim might avoid obscenity charges
Local variation in what is considered ‘patently offensive’

nodes.label: Child Sexual Abuse Laws (18 U.S.C. §2256 et seq.)
nodes.description: Federal statutes banning child pornography or any sexual depiction of minors, with severe criminal penalties for production, distribution, or possession.

properties.context: Includes definitions for CSAM, mandatory reporting to NCMEC, and zero-tolerance approach. Child sexual content is never protected speech.
examples: 18 U.S.C. 2251-2258 dealing with production, distribution, reporting
State-level equivalents criminalizing any child sexual imagery
edge_cases: Animated child porn still prosecuted if obscene
Minor sexting complexities (some states reduce penalties but still illegal federally)

nodes.label: FCC Indecency Rules (18 U.S.C. §1464)
nodes.description: FCC restricts indecent sexual content on public airwaves (radio/TV) during hours when children may be present. Fines for violations.

properties.context: Material doesn't meet the obscenity threshold but is still considered offensive for general broadcast. Cable/Internet are not bound by these rules, but many networks self-regulate.
examples: Network show with partial nudity at 8pm draws FCC complaints
Profanity or graphic sexual talk on daytime radio
edge_cases: Educational vs. prurient content (e.g., anatomy documentary in prime time)
Streaming platforms labeling content with disclaimers

nodes.label: Record-Keeping (18 U.S.C. §2257)
nodes.description: Requires producers of sexually explicit content to verify and keep records proving all performers are adults (18+).

properties.context: Aimed at preventing underage appearances in porn. Primary producers check IDs; secondary distributors also must maintain compliance statements. Subject to DOJ inspections.
examples: Porn studios storing IDs of all performers
Adult websites displaying a 2257 compliance notice
edge_cases: User-generated sites uncertain if considered 'secondary producers'
Foreign producers distributing content in the U.S. might face liability

nodes.label: Age Verification (e.g., LA Act 440)
nodes.description: State laws requiring porn sites to verify user age (18+) before granting access, aimed at limiting minor exposure.

properties.context: Some states impose ID checks for adult websites. Non-compliance can result in civil liability if minors view explicit content. Emergent area with privacy concerns.
examples: Sites requesting driver's license upload for age verification
Blocking entire states to avoid complex compliance
edge_cases: VPN bypass to circumvent age gates
Potential conflict with user privacy / anonymity

nodes.label: Revenge Porn Statutes (Varies by State)
nodes.description: Criminalizes sharing private sexual images without consent to harass or embarrass. Most U.S. states have such laws, with possible civil remedies for victims.

properties.context: A patchwork of state-level laws penalizing distribution of non-consensual intimate material. Overlaps with harassment, extortion, privacy rights. Often called ‘image-based sexual abuse.’
examples: Posting an ex-partner's nudes on the internet for revenge
Threatening to release intimate images to coerce or blackmail
edge_cases: If the subject initially consented to photography but not public dissemination
Deepfake porn of a real individual (some states explicitly ban it, others do not yet)

nodes.label: FOSTA-SESTA
nodes.description: U.S. legislation making it easier to target websites that facilitate sex trafficking or prostitution, amending Section 230 immunity.

properties.context: Removes platform immunity if they 'promote or facilitate prostitution.' Intended to curb sex trafficking but also impacts consensual adult content. Platforms must remove suspect content.
examples: Shutdown of personal ads sections post-FOSTA
Increased moderation of escort or adult service listings
edge_cases: Separating legal sex work discussion vs. trafficking facilitation
Chilling effect on legitimate adult communities or harm reduction sites

nodes.label: Communications Decency Act - Section 230
nodes.description: U.S. law providing immunity from liability for providers of an interactive computer service who publish information provided by others.

properties.context: Historically protected platforms from being liable for user-generated content. FOSTA-SESTA narrowed this protection regarding sex trafficking or prostitution.
examples: Social networks not directly liable for user posts with nudity or adult content
Exemptions if platform is found complicit in illegal activity
edge_cases: Ambiguity over content moderation decisions and how they affect immunity
Future reforms or expansions may further limit Section 230 protections

nodes.label: State-Level Obscenity and Morality Laws
nodes.description: Varying state laws regulating obscene content and nudity based on local community standards.

properties.context: States adopt local definitions of obscenity consistent with the Miller test. Some jurisdictions ban certain sexual acts or displays more stringently.
examples: A state law banning the sale of adult magazines in particular counties
Restrictions on adult video stores near schools or churches
edge_cases: One county’s moral standard may differ from another’s
Online distribution complicates geographic enforcement

nodes.label: Digital Millennium Copyright Act
nodes.description: U.S. copyright law addressing digital rights management and copyright infringement liability.

properties.context: Applies if nude or sexual content is also copyrighted (e.g. professional photography). Platforms may receive takedown requests for copyrighted adult content. Doesn’t directly govern the legality of nudity itself.
examples: Adult film studio filing a DMCA claim to remove pirated clips
Photographer issuing takedown for unauthorized nude images
edge_cases: User claims ‘fair use’ but the content is purely re-uploaded porn
Overlap with non-consensual content where copyright might be a separate removal path

nodes.label: Federal Communications Commission Regulations
nodes.description: U.S. broadcasting regulations that restrict indecent and obscene content on public airwaves.

properties.context: Enforces 18 U.S.C. §1464 and related rules on broadcast radio/TV. Nudity or explicit sex in prime-time can result in fines. Cable, satellite, streaming are not fully bound by these but still often adopt similar guidelines.
examples: FCC fining a network for airing a sexually explicit music video at 7 p.m.
Restricting F-words or explicit references to sexual acts on live TV
edge_cases: ‘Safe harbor’ from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. allows more adult content
Artistic or fleeting nudity might be less penalized

nodes.label: Advertising Standards Authority Code of Non-broadcast Advertising and Direct & Promotional Marketing
nodes.description: UK advertising standards that govern content in non-broadcast media.

properties.context: While primarily UK-focused, it can influence global marketing guidelines for nudity in ads. Nudity or sexual content in promotional materials can be restricted or must meet decency standards.
examples: Banned risqué billboard featuring near-nude model in the UK
Complaint-based system responding to public offense or harm
edge_cases: Ads for adult products that show partial nudity
Difference in local vs. global ad campaigns

nodes.label: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act
nodes.description: U.S. federal law restricting the collection of personal information from children under 13.

properties.context: Focused on data privacy, but relevant if a platform is child-directed. Nudity or explicit content is disallowed on sites aimed at children. Strict parental consent rules for data collection.
examples: Kid-focused websites cannot host adult or nude content at all
Apps requiring parental consent for any user under 13
edge_cases: Mixed-audience sites must have robust age screens or content filters
Over-collection of data from minors might violate COPPA even if no nudity is shown

nodes.label: Prosecutorial Remedies ... (PROTECT Act)
nodes.description: U.S. law prohibiting virtual child pornography and strengthening child exploitation laws.

properties.context: Criminalizes obscene computer-generated imagery of minors (if it visually depicts minors in sexual acts). Expands the definition of child porn to include simulated or digital forms that are indistinguishable from real children.
examples: CGI cartoons showing minors in explicit acts, prosecuted under obscenity provisions
Court expansions to handle AI child porn that looks real
edge_cases: Purely fantasy-like cartoons sometimes disputed if they do not look real
The 'appears to be' standard can trigger legal action if it’s close enough
